title: SignedGateToken
description: The ONE unified Gate Token — the ephemeral, signed, single-operation credential a Gate verifies before any privileged access (GATE_SPEC §7). Minted just-in-time from a durable Grant by an ISSUER (Govern today; a human approver in a future HITL flow), scoped to one `(contract, instance, resource, op)` and expiring in seconds. This single token type REPLACES the former KAT / LAT / MAT: those were the same artifact scoped for different gate kinds, and the kind already lives in `scope.contract`. Kind-specific per-op limits (an llm token's token-caps + prompt-binding, a write token's row cap) ride as the open `constraints` block, so the polymorphism that made the LAT look different lives there, not in a separate token species. SIGNING (carry-canonical convention, matches the Operation Manifest + the gate receipt): Govern signs the EXACT canonical bytes carried in `token_canonical_b64` with Ed25519; the Gate decodes + verifies THOSE bytes against the pinned Govern key and MUST NOT re-canonicalize `token` (canonicalization drift is a security hole). The Gate confirms the token's scope covers the requested `(contract, instance, resource, op)` under the declared match mode; a request no token covers is refused by Govern at dispatch, before the Gate is called (deny before I/O, §6.2). This is a STANDALONE signed envelope (not a member of the codegen'd *AT family in scripts/signed-envelope-family.manifest.ts): its inner `issuer` is intentionally a free identity + `issuer_kind` discriminator so a future human issuer is additive, whereas the family fixes `issuer` to the const `ekka-govern`.

schema.description: Wire discriminator for the signed Gate Token envelope.

signing_alg.description: Signature algorithm. Today only Ed25519 is supported — declared explicitly so a future algorithm migration is a wire-level discriminator change, not a silent reinterpretation.

key_id.description: Identifier of the Ed25519 key that produced `signature_b64`. The Gate resolves this to the anchored Govern signing key (GATE_SPEC §7.4). Enables key rotation — a verifier may hold multiple keys keyed by `key_id`.

signature_b64.description: Base64-encoded Ed25519 signature over decode(token_canonical_b64) under the key identified by `key_id`.

token.description: The decoded inner token, inlined for readability + schema validation. MUST byte-match decode(token_canonical_b64). Verification is against the canonical bytes, never against a re-serialization of this object.

token_canonical_b64.description: Base64-encoded canonical JSON of `token` — the EXACT bytes signed. Verifiers MUST check `signature_b64` against these bytes, NOT against a re-canonicalization of `token`.

GateToken.description: Inner claim of a Gate Token. Carries the identity/lifetime header, the authorization scope `(contract, instance, resource, op)`, and an optional kind-specific `constraints` block. No backend payload appears here — the token authorizes; the native payload travels in the action request and is constrained by the Gate.

token_id.description: Issuance id for this token. The gate receipt's `token_id` MUST equal this value, binding the attestation to the credential that authorized it.

issuer.description: Identity of the party that minted this token. `ekka-govern` when Govern issues at dispatch; a human principal identifier under a future step-up / HITL approval flow. The Gate does not enforce against this value directly — it trusts the anchored signer (`key_id`) — but records it for audit.

issuer_kind.description: What kind of issuer minted the token. `govern` today (Govern at dispatch, after confirming a Grant covers the request); `human` reserved for a future HITL approver. Modeled now so a human issuer is an additive change, not a wire break.

issued_at.description: Issuance timestamp. Verifiers compare against `expires_at` and a local now() with bounded skew (±30s, §7.4).

expires_at.description: Expiry timestamp. Verifiers MUST reject when now() > expires_at (±30s skew). Short TTL — seconds — is the revocation lever; Gates are stateless wrt revocation.

tenant_id.description: Tenant the token was issued under. The Gate MUST check the request tenant context matches.

run_id.description: The run this token is bound to. Free-form string — Govern may choose its own run-id format; non-UUID ids must still verify.

scope.description: The authorization scope. A Gate MUST reject (SCOPE_MISMATCH) any request the scope does not cover under the Gate's declared match mode; the scope MUST be ⊆ the covering Grant (containment, §7.3).

constraints.description: Optional, OPEN for most token kinds, kind-specific per-op limits. Examples: an `llm` token's `token_caps` + `prompt_binding`; a write token's row cap. Absent means no per-op limit beyond the scope. This is where the polymorphism that once distinguished the LAT lives; it MUST NOT carry anything a verifier needs to establish scope (scope is authoritative). On an API-gate token (`scope.contract` `ekka.gate.api.v1`) it is CLOSED: the covering grant's limits under ONE key, `grant`, exactly as the grant stores them, and beside it the reserved call-level field `body_sha256` when the call pins its body. A grant key can never collide with the pin. For a desk grant (`api.write` on `apis/desks`) `grant` is exactly governance/grant-constraints/desks.v1.schema.json.

binding_fingerprint.description: Optional. The fingerprint of the ALIAS BINDING this token was pinned to at grant time — a hash over the canonical alias record (alias design §2.4). Present only for gates that use the alias resource model (absent for first-party gates that do not). When present, the Gate MUST recompute the fingerprint of the alias it resolves at execution and reject (fail closed) on mismatch, so a silently re-pointed alias cannot be acted on under an old authorization. Carried through Grant → token → receipt without Govern ever seeing the concrete resource name.

grant.description: The covering grant's limits, exactly as the grant stores them. Absent when the grant has none.

body_sha256.description: Reserved, call-level: the sha256 of this call's body. Set by Govern per call, never by a grant.

TokenScope.description: The coarse authorization tuple `(contract, instance, resource, op)`, plus the OPTIONAL `capability` this token was minted under (reserved, see that field). EKKA authorizes at this granularity only; the actual operation is the backend's native payload, opaque to Govern and confined by the Gate (GATE_SPEC principle 1).

contract.description: The Gate's interface identity + version, e.g. `ekka.gate.postgres.v1`, `ekka.gate.slack.v1`, `ekka.gate.llm.v1`. There is no `ekka.connector.*` / `ekka.ai_gateway.*` (GATE_SPEC §9.1, §16).

instance.description: The Govern-assigned CANONICAL instance id this token is scoped to (not a tenant-chosen alias; Govern resolves alias → canonical instance at mint time). Grants, tokens, and receipts all bind to this. For a call through the API gate (`ekka.gate.api.v1`) it is the organization's API-gate instance, and `resource` names the connection, for example `apis/desks`.

resource.description: A resource SELECTOR in the Gate's declared namespace (leaf when the op is single-target; a prefix/single-level-glob pattern when the op is inherently set-valued). Always ⊆ the covering Grant's selector. Canonical selector definition: common/resource-selector.schema.json (GATE_SPEC §9.3); pattern inlined here so the generated validator is self-contained.

op.description: The authorization verb, e.g. `read`, `list`, `write`, `invoke`, `complete`. Drawn from the reserved op set, extensible per-gate via the GateDeclaration. MUST be one of the ops the Gate advertises for `resource`.

capability.description: OPTIONAL, RESERVED (GATE_SPEC 1.3.0): accepted by this schema, NOT YET MINTED by Govern. The capability code of the Grant this token was minted from, e.g. `file.fs.extract`, `knowledge.postgres.read`. `op` names the verb the request performs; this names the authority it was issued under, and the two are not interchangeable. GATE_SPEC §7.3 already requires the scope to be ⊆ the covering Grant, but a verifier holding only `op` cannot check that containment: an authorized and an unauthorized request carry an identical `op`. Absent means a token minted before this field existed, and a verifier MUST NOT infer authority from its absence.
